entry.title: Help make things right after calm
entry.summary: After everyone is calm, help your child take a small part in addressing what happened. You can model an apology without requiring them to say one.
entry.cue: Someone has been hurt, belongings were damaged, or a mess needs attention after a difficult moment.
detail: Davies pairs acceptance of feelings with helping make things right. A child can join you to check on another person, offer a tissue, or help gather things that were thrown.
Young toddlers need adult help with this. A sincere apology modeled by you can say more than a required “sorry.” The conversation can also make room for what was difficult for your child.

references.locator: Calm first, practical repair, checking on another person and adult modeling rather than forced apology
